description: Check whether a gutter can carry the runoff from your roof in a design storm, and how many downspouts it needs. Uses the USDA NRCS gutter and downspout capacity table and your local rainfall intensity. Formula: Runoff Q (cfs) = roof area (sq ft) × rainfall intensity (in/hr) ÷ 43,200 (12 in/ft × 3,600 s/hr); gpm = cfs × 448.8. The gutter is adequate when Q ≤ its NRCS PA-1 capacity at your slope. Downspouts = the larger of ⌈Q ÷ one downspout's PA-1 capacity⌉ and ⌈run length ÷ max length per downspout⌉. Max roof area for the gutter = capacity × 43,200 ÷ intensity.

max_run_per_downspout_ft.description: Max gutter length per downspout (SMACNA practical max 50 ft) (ft); default 50

rain_in_per_hr.description: Design rainfall intensity (5-minute depth from NOAA Atlas 14 × 12) (in/hr); default 6

roof_area_sqft.description: Roof area draining to this gutter (plan view, not slope length) (sq ft); default 1200

name: calc_gutter_size
title: Gutter & Downspout Size Calculator (Roof Runoff, Gutter Capacity, Number of Downspouts)
